text:
Nadia: quick alert — new canary (nightingale-q4-int4) shows a weird class of funcall parse hits where the assembler reconstructs multiple top-level objects because slice boundaries split arrays. Example below.
Evan: paste the minimal repro
Nadia: logs:
```
INVOKE id=yy42 slice=9/40 model=nightingale-q4
OUT >> {"tool":"catalog.search","items":[{"id":10,"score":0.95},
...<slice ends>...
---next slice---
INVOKE continue id=yy42 slice=10/40
OUT >> {"id":11,"score":0.91}],"meta":{}}
parser: JSONError: unexpected token '{' near beginning
```
Clara: sounds like our stream merger is treating each slice as independent JSON. We should ensure the streaming assembler buffers until top-level braces balanced before handing to the parser.
stitch-bot: canary metrics: baseline parse errors 0.6% -> canary 3.4% (n=1500). error breakdown: 46% unexpected token, 38% unexpected EOF, 16% other.
Evan: short fixes to try: 1) assembler wait-for-balanced-braces flag (cheap) 2) overlapping-token replay (prepend last 12 tokens of previous slice) 3) sentinel suffix in prompt for toolcalls 4) small tokenizer diff to pick overlap size
Nadia: prioritizing: assembler buffering + tokenizer diff. if buffering reduces >70% we can keep. otherwise fall back to overlap.
koji: I'll add a toggle in runtime to enable "buffer-until-balanced" and run a 30m micro-canary with reduced slice count. Also adding telemetry tags: "reassembly:buffered" and "reassembly:overlap_attempt".
Clara: also add a short postprocess repair that, on unexpected token, tries to join the trailing/leading fragments and re-parse before marking as failure — for diagnostics only.
Evan: please attach 50 failed payloads to the ticket RF-9187. Nadia: can you coordinate collection?
Nadia: will do and report back with micro-canary numbers. Keeping thread for raw payload dumps and flags toggles.
